en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Section on the Puzzling Questions, Chapter on Omniscient Knowledge.
9. The Question on the Fearlessness of the Arahant “Venerable Nāgasena, this has been said by the Blessed One:
‘The Arahants are free from fear and terror.’”

Furthermore, in the city of Rājagaha, having seen the elephant Dhanapālaka charging toward the Blessed One, five hundred arahants who had destroyed the taints abandoned him and fled in every direction—leaving behind only the Elder Ānanda.

"Venerable Nāgasena, why did those arahants flee? Did they flee out of fear, thinking 'He will be known by his own deed' and wishing to strike down the One of Ten Powers, or was it because of the Tathāgata’s incomparable, vast, and peerless miracle?"
"Did they depart because they wished to see [him]?
If, venerable Nāgasena, it was said by the Blessed One that 'Arahants are free from fear and terror,' then how is it that [they fled] in the city...?"
The statement that “Ānanda [fled]” is false. For if,
upon seeing the elephant Dhanapālaka charging at the Blessed One in the city of Rājagaha, five hundred arahants—
having abandoned the Best of Conquerors and fled in every direction— did so with the sole exception of the Elder Ānanda, then by that...
"For it would be false even to say, 'The Arahants are free from fear and anxiety.
This too is a dilemma with two horns that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
"Indeed, Great King, this was also spoken by the Blessed One:"
Regarding the statement, “The Arahants are free from fear and terror”: when the Blessed One saw the elephant Dhanapālaka charging toward him in the city of Rājagaha,
five hundred of those whose taints were destroyed abandoned him and fled in every direction—
leaving behind only the Elder Ānanda— not out of fear, nor with the desire to cause the Blessed One to fall.
"But that cause, Great King, by which Arahants might fear or be terrified has been utterly cut off in Arahants; therefore, Arahants are free from fear and trembling.
Does the great earth, Great King, fear even when it is being dug, split open, or supported by the ocean, mountains, and mountain peaks?"
“No indeed, Bhante.
“For what reason, Great King?
“Because, Bhante, there is no cause by which the great earth would fear or be terrified.”
“In the same way, great king, there is no cause by which Arahants would feel fear or terror.
Does a mountain peak, great king, feel fear when it is being cut, or broken, or falling, or being consumed by fire?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.”
“For what reason, Great King?
“Venerable sir, there is no cause for a mountain peak to fear or be terrified.
“In the same way, Great King, there is no cause for Arahants to fear or be terrified.”

Even if, Great King, all those included within the categories of beings throughout a hundred thousand world-systems were to run toward a single Arhat with swords in hand and attempt to terrify him, there would be no alteration whatsoever in the mind of the Arhat.
Why is that? Because it is impossible and out of the question.
Moreover, Great King, it occurred to those whose taints were exhausted as follows:
“Today, when the most excellent of men, the supreme bull of the Conquerors, has entered this noble city, the elephant Dhanapālaka will charge through the street;
there is no doubt that the attendant will not abandon the God of Gods. If we all do not abandon the Blessed One, [it will be the same for] Ānanda.”
‘The virtue of Ānanda will not become manifest, and the elephant-nāga will not approach the Tathāgata; come now,
let us depart, so that this great body of people may be released from the bonds of defilement,
and the virtue of Ānanda may become manifest.’”
“Thus, having seen this benefit, those Arahants departed toward the cardinal and intermediate directions.

“Very well analyzed, venerable Nāgasena, is the question. It is even so: there is no fear or terror for the Arahants; it is because they have seen a benefit that the Arahants have departed toward the cardinal and intermediate directions.
The ninth problem: On the Fearlessness of the Arahants.
